bib.title: BLEURT: Learning Robust Metrics for Text Generation
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL)

question: Can a learned, BERT-based reference-based metric for text generation be made both accurate on human ratings and robust to domain and quality drift?
hypothesis: Pre-training BERT on millions of synthetic sentence pairs with lexical and semantic supervision signals, before fine-tuning on human ratings, makes the metric generalize when training data is scarce, skewed or out-of-domain.
contributions: BLEURT, a BERT-based learned metric fine-tuned on a few thousand human ratings
A pre-training scheme using about 6.5 million synthetic perturbations of 1.8 million Wikipedia segments with 9 supervision tasks
State-of-the-art results on WMT Metrics 2017-2019 (to-English) and WebNLG 2017, plus robustness tests under quality drift

method.summary: BERT (Large or Base, uncased) is further pre-trained on synthetic (reference, perturbed) pairs with a multi-task regression/classification loss over 9 signals (BLEU, ROUGE P/R/F, BERTscore P/R/F, 4 backtranslation likelihoods, MNLI entailment, backtranslation flag), then fine-tuned with an L2 regression head on the [CLS] vector to predict human ratings. Evaluated by agreement with human ratings on WMT17-19, a skewed WMT17 drift benchmark and WebNLG.
method.task: learned reference-based sentence-level evaluation metric for NLG (translation, data-to-text)

datasets.name: Synthetic Wikipedia perturbations
datasets.size: 1.8 million Wikipedia segments, about 6.5 million perturbations
datasets.source: Wikipedia; perturbed by BERT mask-filling (up to 15 masks, beam 8), backtranslation (en-de Transformer), word dropping (about 30% of data)

datasets.name: WMT Metrics Shared Task 2017-2019 (to-English)
datasets.size: training sets of 5,360, 9,492 and 147,691 records for 2017, 2018, 2019
datasets.split: For each year, test sets of previous years used for training and validation; 10% validation for 2017 and 2018, 5% for 2019, no source leakage
datasets.source: WMT news-domain human ratings (Pearson on standardized ratings 2017; DARR 2018, 2019)

datasets.name: WMT17 skewed subsets
datasets.size: 11.9% of the original 5,344 training records at alpha 3.0 (50.7%, 30.3%, 20.4% for 0.5, 1.0, 1.5)
datasets.split: 10 equal bins; train sampled with prob 1/B^alpha, test with 1/(11-B)^alpha

datasets.name: WebNLG 2017 human assessments
datasets.split: 0% to about 50% to training, split by system or by RDF input
datasets.source: WebNLG Challenge 2017 (Shimorina et al. 2019); ratings for semantics, grammar, fluency
datasets.preprocessing: null values removed; highest score over multiple references

models.name: BLEURT -pre / BLEURTbase -pre
models.architecture: BERT fine-tuned directly on ratings, no synthetic pre-training

models.name: sentBLEU, BERTscore (BERT-large, roBERTa), MoverScore, chrF++, BEER, Meteor++, RUSE, YiSi1, ESIM, TER

training.objective: pre-training: weighted sum of per-task L2 (regression) and cross-entropy (classification) losses; fine-tuning: L2 regression on human rating
training.epochs: inferred: about 2 epochs over synthetic data in 400,000 steps (Appendix B.4)
training.regularisation: checkpoint with best Kendall Tau on held-out validation chosen, evaluated every 1,500 steps
training.hardware: Google Cloud TPUs v2 for learning; Nvidia Tesla V100 for evaluation and test

other.task_weights: gamma_k set by grid search on WMT17 validation, grouped (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTscore), (4 backtranslation likelihoods), (entail, backtrans flag); values not given
other.three_step: BERT pre-training, synthetic pre-training, fine-tuning; WebNLG BLEURT -wmt was fine-tuned on synthetic then WebNLG; BLEURT on synthetic, WMT 16-18, then WebNLG

inference.samples: single run per configuration; no seeds or variance reported

metrics.name: Kendall Tau
metrics.definition: agreement of metric with human ratings, no filter

metrics.name: Pearson r (WMT17 official)
metrics.definition: on standardized human judgments across segments

metrics.name: DARR / DA (WMT18-19 official)
metrics.definition: (Concordant - Discordant)/(Concordant + Discordant) over translation pairs of one reference, discarding pairs less than 25 points apart on a 100-point scale

eval.protocol: Own implementation of the WMT benchmark (small differences from official results marked with * in 2018); no significance tests or seeds.

evidence.quote: We use batch size 32, learning rate 1e-5, and 800,000 steps for pre-training and 40,000 steps for ﬁne-tuning.

results.claim: BLEURT (BERT-large) has the highest average Kendall Tau on WMT17 to-English, ahead of BERTscore and sentBLEU
results.baseline_value: BERTscore w/ BERT 53.3; w/ roBERTa 58.0; sentBLEU 32.4
results.setup: WMT17 to-English, BLEURT fine-tuned on WMT15-16 ratings
results.table: Table 2, row BLEURT, column avg tau

results.claim: Pre-training adds up to 7.4 Kendall Tau points on WMT17 for BLEURTbase (zh-en)
results.setup: WMT17 zh-en, BLEURTbase with vs without pre-training
results.quote: it adds up to 7.4 Kendall Tau points for BLEURTbase (zh-en)

results.claim: On WMT18 and WMT19 the pre-training effect is milder, up to 2.1 points
BLEURT average Kendall Tau on WMT18 and WMT19
results.table: Table 3, row BLEURT, column avg tau
results.note: WMT19 avg tau is 33.8 vs 32.0 for BERTscore w/ roBERTa (Table 4)

results.claim: Without pre-training, BLEURT falls below BERTscore at skew 1.0 and below sentBLEU at skew >= 1.5; pre-trained BLEURT falls below baselines only at skew 3.0
results.setup: WMT17 resampled with skew factor alpha, BERT-large, vs sentBLEU and BERTscore; values read from Fig 2 only

results.claim: At the most extreme skew only 11.9% of the 5,344 WMT17 training records remain
results.quote: we use only 11.9% of the original 5,344 training records

results.claim: On WebNLG, BLEURT -wmt is competitive with BERTscore with as little as 836 training records, and full BLEURT is comparable with zero WebNLG fine-tuning; vanilla BERT needs about a third of the data
results.setup: WebNLG 2017, 3 rating tasks, BERT-large; split by input
results.quote: BLEURT -wmt is competitive with as little as 836 records

results.claim: Ablation: pre-training on BERTscore, entailment and backtranslation signals helps; BLEU and ROUGE signals hurt
results.setup: WMT17, relative Kendall Tau change, single-task and leave-one-out, read from Fig 4

results.claim: Most pre-training gains arrive in the first 400,000 steps, about 2 epochs over the synthetic data
results.setup: WMT17, fine-tuned after varying pre-training steps
results.quote: Most gains are obtained during the ﬁrst 400,000 steps

limits: Authors leave open whether to drop BLEU and ROUGE signals, since they hurt on WMT17 but may help on other tasks
WMT18 and 19 test sets are noisy; own re-implementation of benchmark differs slightly from official results
No seeds, variance or significance tests reported; task weights not listed
Drift results are on a synthetic skew of WMT17, not real drift
Future work named: multilingual evaluation and hybrid human-classifier methods

terms.definition: measures how much the training data is left-skewed and the test data is right-skewed

Xenouleas et al.; fine-tunes BERT for quality estimation
